fear.name: Despair
fear.hint: The Despair pool of the GM.

forcePrivateRolls.name: Force private player rolls
forcePrivateRolls.hint: Every player roll is whispered to that player and the GMs only. Players never see each other's dice.

enforceAnonymity.name: Keep character sheets anonymous
enforceAnonymity.hint: Stops default ownership on a character from being raised above None, so players cannot open each other's sheets. Each player still owns their own character.

searchTokensPerRoom.name: Search tokens per room
searchTokensPerRoom.hint: How many times a single room can be searched during one time of day.

lockRollDialog.name: Lock the roll window for players
lockRollDialog.hint: Players cannot change the dice, the trait, advantage, experiences or the situational bonus — those come from the action, a Hope Call or the GM. Selecting an experience also stops silently charging Hope, since spending it is the Experience Hope Call. GMs are unaffected.

roomVisibility.name: Players only see who is in their room
roomVisibility.hint: Hides other characters' tokens unless they are in the same room region. Walls and vision get most of the way there; this closes the gaps for doorways, open archways and scenes built without walls. GMs always see everything.

lockPlayerResources.name: Players cannot edit Actions, Hope or traits
lockPlayerResources.hint: Those change through play — spending an action, resting, earning an advancement — so players cannot set them by hand. HP and Stress stay editable, since players mark their own damage. GMs are unaffected.

chargeMovement.name: Crossing rooms costs a Move
chargeMovement.hint: Moving inside a room is free. Crossing into another Scene Region spends the free Move for that time of day, then an action. Turn off to handle movement by hand.

despairFromRolls.name: Rolls grant Despair
despairFromRolls.hint: When a player's roll lands with Despair, add 1 to the pool of the Monokuma who looks after that student. Use the gear on the Despair widget to divide the students up.

hideSystemFear.name: Replace the Daggerheart Fear tracker
hideSystemFear.hint: Hides Daggerheart's single shared Fear bar and uses one Despair pool per Monokuma instead, as the guide requires. Turn off to go back to the system tracker.

pixelFont.name: Pixel font
pixelFont.hint: Uses Press Start 2P for interface chrome — HUD, Despair, character name, trait labels and tabs. Journals, chat bodies and editable fields keep the normal face so long text stays readable.

debug.name: Verbose console logging
debug.hint: Print Danganronpa RPG diagnostics to the browser console. Affects this client only.

Guard.blocked: Only the GM can change that. Actions, Hope and traits move through play — spend an action, take a rest, earn an advancement.

Assign.title: Which Monokuma carries which student
Assign.intro: A roll that lands with Despair feeds the pool of that student's Monokuma. The guide has the GMs split the roster strictly between them.
Assign.failed: The division could not be saved. See the console for details.
Assign.noMonokumas: There are no full Gamemasters to assign students to. Assistant GMs do not get a Despair pool.
Assign.implicitHint: Never assigned explicitly — currently falling back to the first Monokuma.
Assign.footnote: * = not assigned yet, using the fallback. Choose “— nobody —” to keep a student out of every Despair pool (a Mastermind, an NPC-run character, or a template).

Despair.pipTooltip: Set {name}'s Despair to {n}. Click the last filled one to spend it.
Despair.notEnough: Not enough Despair for {call}: it costs {cost} and you hold {held}.

Action.failed: That action could not be completed. See the console for details.
Action.costMove: free once per time of day
Action.noRoom: This token is not inside a room region, so there is nothing to search. Put the token in a room, or ask the GM.
Action.tokensLeft: {room}: {n} search token(s) left this time of day.
Action.moveFree: Used the free Move for this time of day.
Action.movePaid: No free Move left, so this one cost an action.
Action.observeCrit: Critical — a Truth Bullet with its category identified, plus a substantial hint from the GM.
Action.observeGm: Total {total}. The GM compares this against the Observe table for whatever you are looking at. A failure costs 2 Stress.
Action.searchGoalHint: The guide lets you declare what you are searching for. What you find still depends on the room and the roll.
Action.dynamicHint: Describe what you are doing and the GM picks a difficulty. Dynamic actions have gentler thresholds than the standard ones — that is the reward for inventing something.
Action.dynamicDescribe: Describe what your character is doing. The GM reads this and sets the difficulty.
Action.dynamicPlaceholder: e.g. I water the plants in the garden, looking for anything buried.
Action.dynamicSetBy: Now set the difficulty and the trait for this attempt:
Action.dynamicDescription: You describe something your character does that no standard action covers — watering the garden, rigging a scoreboard, anything. The GM sets the difficulty and the trait. Dynamic actions use gentler thresholds and an inverted Remnant scale, deliberately rewarding invention over routine.
Action.noRoomNote: Your token is not inside a room region.
Action.callsGmNote: This one is judged by the GM — your roll and request are sent to them.
Action.gmPrompt: {action} — what are you trying to do? The GM sees this along with your roll.

placeholder.think: e.g. Who could have got into the pool room unseen?
placeholder.listen: e.g. Listening at the door to the kitchen.
placeholder.analyze: e.g. Analysing the torn cloth from the hallway.
placeholder.observe: e.g. Looking for anything around the body.
placeholder.directMurder: Who, where, and how — as agreed beforehand.

Action.analyzeGm: The GM compares this against the Analyze table for that Truth Bullet. A failure locks it for you until the end of the chapter.
Action.murderConfirm: This opens a direct murder. It requires prior agreement with the GM and the consent of the player involved. The action is spent even if the conditions are not met.
Action.murderPrompt: Confirm the plan for the GM: your victim, the room, and anything you are relying on.
Action.sabotageSeen: {actor} is seen doing something to a project in {room}.
Action.sabotageWatched: {actor} is doing something to {project} in {room}, and everyone present can see roughly what.
Action.sabotageCarryOn: Carry on anyway? You have spent nothing yet.

Analyze.prompt: Analyse a Truth Bullet to identify what it really is, or simply ask the GM for a hint.
Analyze.noBullets: You are not carrying any Truth Bullets yet, so only a hint is available.

Inventory.full: You are already carrying the most {category} you can ({limit}). Drop one first.
Inventory.notCarried: (not picked up — that category is full)

Remnant.reinforced: That Remnant is reinforced and cannot be removed.
Remnant.revealWarning: Remnants are the GM's notes and normally stay hidden — players get Truth Bullets instead. Revealing this shows it on the map.
Remnant.searchNote: {actor} searched {room} for a {category} (rolled {total}) and came away with {item} — Tier {tier}.
Remnant.sabotageWorked: It worked: the project is frozen until {repair} is finished.
Remnant.sabotageFailed: It failed — the project is untouched, but the attempt left a trace.
Remnant.projectNote: {actor} worked on {project} in {room}, gaining {progress} progress, and rolled {total} to cover their tracks.

Rest.noRegions: This scene has no room regions yet. Draw regions on the Regions layer first.

Calls.noPool: This Monokuma has no Despair pool. Give a GM ownership of the actor, or check the Despair bar.

Project.heading: Projects
Project.title: Project
Project.choosePrompt: Start something new, or push a project that already exists?
Project.startPrompt: Describe the project for the GM: what you want to build or achieve, and where.
Project.startPlaceholder: e.g. Build a hidden compartment under the library floor.
Project.agreedWarning: This assumes you have already agreed the project with the GM. Creating one you have not discussed is how you end up with it deleted mid-session.
Project.startNote: The project is created immediately and appears in Projects. The GM is notified and can adjust the scale, the room, or remove it.
Project.startedOk: "{name}" created and added to Projects. The GM has been told.
Project.indirectMine: This is an indirect murder (kept secret — only you and the GMs will see it)
Project.gmCanAdjust: Created by a player. Adjust the scale, room or secrecy from the Projects gear, or delete it.
Project.repaired: repaired. {name} can be worked on again.
Project.frozenNow: {name} is broken and frozen until {repair} is finished.
Project.alreadyFrozen: {name} is already broken and waiting on a repair.
Project.nothingToSabotage: Nothing here can be sabotaged. Projects already broken, and repairs themselves, cannot be.
Project.none: There are no projects yet. Start one first.
Project.wrongRoom: Nothing you can work on in {room}. Elsewhere: {names}
Project.aloneBonus: Nobody else is in the room, so the project gains +1 progress.
Project.createNote: Progress only advances when someone uses the Work on Project action — never from attacks or rests. An indirect murder is made secret automatically.
Project.name: Name
Project.manageTooltip: Set which room each project belongs to, and who may see it
Project.manageIntro: A project can be tied to a room, so only characters standing there can work on it or sabotage it.
Project.secretNote: Indirect murder projects are secret by default: only the killer and the GMs see them. Use Share to bring a co-conspirator in.
Project.shareIntro: Let another player see this project. Players can bring in a co-conspirator; GMs can share with anyone.
Project.noPlayers: There are no players to share with.
Project.alreadyFull: {name} is already at {current}/{target}. There is no progress left to add.
Project.alreadyEmpty: {name} is already at 0 progress. There is nothing left to take away.
